businessProblem: Hertz faces near-total revenue collapse from COVID-19 travel demand destruction, with large fleet-financing obligations, high leverage, and severe liquidity pressure as of 15 May 2020. Formal restructuring is being evaluated. Diagnose root causes and recommend highest-priority action plan.

evidence.finding: Revenue severely impaired by near-total COVID-19 travel demand collapse beginning early 2020
evidence.source: Hertz SEC filing / Chapter 11 press release, public reporting May 2020

evidence.finding: Hertz carries large fleet-financing obligations that are contractually rigid and continue regardless of revenue
Liquidity pressure severe — insufficient cash to service debt and fleet-financing at collapsed revenue levels
High pre-existing leverage compounds the revenue shock impact
Fleet utilization near zero due to travel restrictions — core revenue-generating asset is idle
Fleet disposal is an option but used-vehicle market prices are depressed in the crisis environment
COVID-19 travel demand collapse duration unknown — recovery timeline deeply uncertain as of May 2020
evidence.source: Industry reporting, government travel restriction data

evidence.finding: Management evaluating formal restructuring options including Chapter 11 — no formal decision yet as of 15 May 2020

ownerConstraintProfile.managementCapability: MEDIUM — experienced but facing unprecedented external shock
ownerConstraintProfile.keyPersonDependency: LOW — public company with distributed governance
ownerConstraintProfile.accountabilityWeakness: MEDIUM — creditor standstill not yet achieved
